supersedes: snapshot_version 1, which carried a single 'corpus_digest' covering only the full-frame cross-check verdicts plus two crop columns. That digest did NOT cover agreement_flag_crop, cross_check_status_crop, resolution_basis_crop, matched_rank_crop or taxonomic_distance_crop, so every verdict written by `recompute-crop-crosscheck` could change while the hash stayed identical. It also omitted matched_rank on the full-frame path. A v1 'corpus_digest' value is NOT comparable with either digest below.
purpose: Stage 0 ground truth for the multi-project refactor (Phase 2 Stages 3-8). Stage 8 must reproduce verdict_digest.sha256 EXACTLY after migrating this database into a project folder and re-running recompute-crosscheck, recompute-crops and recompute-crop-crosscheck. Any difference is a refactor defect, not a finding.

column_classification.note: Every column of the 90-column schema is in exactly one class; this is asserted when the snapshot is generated, so a schema addition fails loudly rather than being silently left out of both digests.

analytical_verdict.note: A decision the pipeline made. A basis/status string counts as a verdict when it is the recorded REASON for a decision and is drawn from a closed vocabulary (crop_basis: 6 distinct values, resolution_basis: 3, tt_banner_basis: 10). It counts as provenance when it records where a value came from (weather_match_source: 137 distinct, capture_time_source).

evidence.note: Raw model or OCR output. Hashed into evidence_digest only.

provenance_metadata.note: Describes HOW, not WHAT. Never hashed. `id`, `ingested_at_utc` and `created_at_utc` differ on any re-import, so hashing them would make the digest fail for reasons that carry no analytical meaning; `agreement_rationale` is prose that can be reworded without a verdict changing.

source_data.note: Parsed from the alert email; not decided by us.

verdict_digest.scope_note: Covers both cross-check paths (full-frame and crop) and the crop decision. Species resolution, capture-time decoding and weather enrichment are also analytical, and are listed under column_classification.analytical_verdict.out_of_scope_for_verdict_digest rather than hashed here. They are excluded deliberately: none is re-run by recompute-crosscheck / recompute-crops / recompute-crop-crosscheck, and backfill-weather calls a live API whose response could differ for reasons unrelated to any refactor -- which would make the gate fail without a defect. Their distributions and per-species counts are recorded above as a separate check.
how_it_is_computed: Absent columns are selected as SQL NULL, so a 52-column and a 90-column database produce comparably shaped rows and comparable digests.
Field encoding: NULL -> JSON null; a float column -> a string formatted '%.6f'; a *_json column -> canonicalised (see below); everything else -> its string value.
Rows are sorted ascending by source_message_id using Python's default str ordering (Unicode code point), NOT SQLite's collation.
Each row is serialised as a JSON array with json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',',':')).
SHA-256 over the concatenation of those lines, each followed by a single b'\n'. Hex digest, lowercase.

evidence_digest.scope_note: Informational, NOT pass/fail. Re-running BioCLIP or the detector is not something the multi-project refactor should be doing at all, so a change here means something re-ran that should not have -- worth investigating, but it is not the migration's acceptance criterion. A stale-but-matching evidence digest alongside a changed verdict digest localises a defect to the decision logic rather than the model.
evidence_digest.canonicalisation: Each *_json value is decoded, every float in it rounded to 6 decimal places recursively, then re-encoded with sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',',':'). A value that does not parse as JSON is hashed as its raw string rather than dropped.

shared_encoding_rationale.why_floats_are_rounded: Fixed 6dp formatting makes the digests reproducible across platforms and BLAS builds, where a last-bit difference carries no analytical meaning. A change large enough to matter at IoU or score scale is far above 1e-6, and the full-precision min/max/mean/quartiles in 'numeric_summaries' remain available as a second, finer check.
shared_encoding_rationale.null_representation: JSON null. Chosen over a sentinel string because no stored value can collide with it -- a literal '<NULL>' in the data could.
